title: Knowledge check: Authentication Testing and Security Review

questions.prompt: In Authentication Testing and Security Review, which statement best describes Testing unauthenticated access?
options: Make behavior reproducible with assertions for a normal case, invalid input, boundary values and errors. Mock external side effects in unit tests and keep separate integration checks for real boundaries.
This option describes a different concept and does not define testing unauthenticated access (choice 2).
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
questions.answer_key: Make behavior reproducible with assertions for a normal case, invalid input, boundary values and errors. Mock external side effects in unit tests and keep separate integration checks for real boundaries.
questions.explanation: Make behavior reproducible with assertions for a normal case, invalid input, boundary values and errors. Mock external side effects in unit tests and keep separate integration checks for real boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Authentication Testing and Security Review?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Authentication answers who is making a request; authorization answers what that identity may do. Hash passwords with established libraries, enforce access on the server, and design sessions/tokens for expiration and revocation.
questions.answer_key: Authentication answers who is making a request; authorization answers what that identity may do. Hash passwords with established libraries, enforce access on the server, and design sessions/tokens for expiration and revocation.
questions.explanation: Authentication answers who is making a request; authorization answers what that identity may do. Hash passwords with established libraries, enforce access on the server, and design sessions/tokens for expiration and revocation.

questions.prompt: A change related to Authentication Testing and Security Review appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
